bottom_line: In AFCAPS/TexCAPS, lovastatin vs placebo reduced first acute major coronary events (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50-0.79).
implications: Based on 183 vs 116 first primary events over an average follow-up of 5.2 years, the trial supports that lovastatin reduced the risk of a first acute major coronary event in this studied primary-prevention population (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50-0.79). The reported data also support LDL-C lowering to 2.96 mmol/L (115 mg/dL) with lovastatin and similar overall mortality (80 vs 77 deaths); the document states the study was not adequately powered to detect differences in cardiovascular or CHD mortality.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled primary prevention trial.
Population was men and women without clinically evident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with average TC/LDL-C and below-average HDL-C.
major_points.quote: men and women without clinically evident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with average total cholesterol (TC) and LDL-C levels and below-average high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels.

major_points.text: Intervention was lovastatin 20-40 mg daily vs placebo on background low–saturated fat, low-cholesterol diet.
major_points.quote: Intervention.—Lovastatin (20-40 mg daily) or placebo in addition to a low– saturated fat, low-cholesterol diet.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was first acute major coronary event (fatal/nonfatal MI, unstable angina, or sudden cardiac death).
major_points.quote: Main Outcome Measures.—First acute major coronary event defined as fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or sudden cardiac death.

major_points.text: Lovastatin reduced primary endpoint events vs placebo with RR 0.63 (95% CI 0.50-0.79).
major_points.quote: lovastatin reduced the incidence of first acute major coronary events (183 vs 116 first events; relative risk [RR], 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.50-0.79; P,.001)

major_points.text: Lovastatin lowered LDL-C by 25% to 2.96 mmol/L (115 mg/dL) and increased HDL-C by 6% to 1.02 mmol/L (39 mg/dL).
major_points.quote: Lovastatin (20-40 mg daily) reduced LDL-C by 25% to 2.96 mmol/L (115 mg/dL) and increased HDL-C by 6% to 1.02 mmol/L (39 mg/dL).

major_points.text: Overall mortality was similar between groups (80 vs 77 deaths).
major_points.quote: The overall mortality rate was similar in each group, with 80 deaths among participants treated with lovastatin and 77 deaths among participants treated with placebo
